newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Congress to consider money laundering measure.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Congress to consider money laundering measure.

text.p: Rep Nydia Velazquez introduced a bill on Tuesday to create a national strategy for combating money laundering and related financial crimes.
The bill, drafted in consultation with the Treasury Department, would require the President to develop goals and operational initiatives to curb money laundering.
The New York Democrat said the bill would allow Treasury to expand a successful program combating money laundering in the Jackson Heights neighborhood of Queens, New York.

"The Treasury Department has worked quickly and decisively to help protect our communities from the effects of money laundering," Velazquez said in a statement. "This bill gives the department the authority to apply those efforts to a comprehensive national strategy."
Fifteen areas would be targeted in the bill, including Los Angeles, New York, Houston, Miami, Atlanta, Chicago, Philadelphia and the Pacific Northwest.
Such regions could be designated "high risk" areas for money laundering, allowing increased federal law enforcement assistance and eligibility for financial crimes grants.
